content.title: About
content.content: Ice cream cake is a dessert that combines layers of soft sponge cake soaked with ice cream and a creamy frosting. It often features multiple ice‑cream flavors, as well as fruit, nuts, or chocolate decorations. Served chilled, it is suitable for celebrations and everyday treats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ice cream cake appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as an alternative to traditional butter cakes.
There are more than 30 popular flavor combinations, ranging from classic vanilla to exotic mango‑coconut.
Cakes are frequently adorned with edible flowers and gold leaf, making them popular at weddings.
In Russia, ice cream cake became widespread in the 2010s thanks to the growth of café‑dessert chains.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base of the ice cream provides calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk and eggs used in the sponge are rich in vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: The custard frosting and dairy base supply a modest amount of protein for tissue repair.

items.title: Antioxidants from fruit layers
items.content: When berries or other fruits are added, they contribute antioxidants that help protect cells.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Ice cream contains lactose, so those with intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Casein and whey proteins can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The cake is often sweet, which may be problematic for people with diabetes or those watching weight.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of the creamy frosting and ice cream, a serving can exceed 400 kcal.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the cake into portions and serve immediately after removing from the freezer. Fresh berries, mint leaves, or grated chocolate can be added to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the ice cream cake in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Before serving, let it sit out for 10–15 minutes to make slicing easier. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 30 minutes, as it will melt.
